title: Football transfer rumours: Lacazette or Aubameyang to Barcelona?
trail: Nahitan Nández to Tottenham? | Maxwel Cornet to Burnley? | Divock Origi to West Ham? | Kyle Hudlin to Manchester City?
body: Barcelona want to sell Martin Braithwaite and sign another striker, and the Spanish newspaper Sport reports that both Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Alexandre Lacazette are on their shortlist, and that Arsenal would be willing to sell either of them. “Barça would only be able to sign one,” warns Sport, “and wouldn’t be able to pay a fee for either player.” The Arsenal suits might stop reading there, and therefore miss the bit about any deal having to be in the form of a player exchange. The Gunners are after a new striker of their own in the shape of Internazionale’s Lautaro Martínez and, if Tuttosport is to be believed, might end up attempting a swoop for both the Argentinian and the club’s former manager, Antonio Conte, unless Mikel Arteta manages to coax a significant improvement out of his team over the next week or two. Tottenham have also been looking to Italy for potential signings, with the London club having contacted Cagliari to ask if they might kindly consider letting them have the Uruguayan midfielder Nahitan Nández. Then there’s the Japanese defender Takehiro Tomiyasu, who has been linked with both Spurs and Leicester, with news that his current employers, Bologna, are showing interest in the Argentinian defender Andres Herrera suggesting they might be preparing to lose the 22-year-old. He wouldn’t be the first defender Spurs have tried to sign this summer – Marca reports that Villarreal’s Pau Torres turned them down because he wants to play in the Champions League. That’s not all that Marca is reporting: on its front page it trumpets news that Real Madrid’s pursuit of Kylian Mbappé has “entered its decisive phase this week”, though inside the tune changes slightly, with the assertion that “we are entering the decisive two weeks”. Either way, this is part of the decisive timeframe. The Spaniards are ready to make an offer but, with the player in the final year of his contract and pressure building in Paris for him to extend, they are “waiting for the tension between Mbappé and PSG to reach a peak before they make their move”. “We need to find quality,” said Sean Dyche after Burnley lost at home against Brighton on the season’s opening weekend, though he added that “nothing is imminent” despite rumours linking them to Maxwel Cornet, among others. They are said to have outbid Hertha Berlin for Cornet with an offer of around £12m, though the player did not exactly encourage their interest as he was sent off in Lyon’s first match of the Ligue 1 season, which they lost 3-0 against Angers on Sunday – the player obviously taking the name of their opponents a little too literally. The Mail points out that Burnley’s last senior signing from a foreign club was Steve Defour from Anderlecht in 2016. The Times also reports that three Premier League clubs are squabbling over Divock Origi, with Wolves, West Ham and Crystal Palace all interested in the Belgian, who joined Liverpool when he was 19, is now 26, has started 63 games for the club in all competitions at the rate of nine a year (though he has been out on loan for some of them), and has very little to show for all those years except quite a lot of medals. Wolves have also been linked with the 24-year-old Guinean midfielder Amadou Diawara, and are said to have had a chat about him with Roma suits while they were in England to discuss Tammy Abraham’s move from Chelsea. Southampton’s pursuit of a new defender following the departure of Jannik Vestergaard has taken them to the door of Gary Cahill, who at 35 is a free agent after leaving Crystal Palace, though the times reports cryptically that “they are in talks with defenders based abroad”. And Manchester City have taken an unexpected interest in the Solihull Moors striker Kyle Hudlin, who could not be less of an obvious fit for Pep Guardiola’s team of nimble, diminutive forwards – the 21-year-old is 6ft 9in, and also on the radar of Middlesbrough and Cardiff.
